Fudgy, dairy-free chocolate cookies with a crackled icing-sugar coat
20 minutes, plus at least 1 hour chilling
for rolling; add more if you run out
Beat the sugar, cocoa and oil on medium speed until smooth and glossy.
Add the eggs one at a time, mixing well after each. Beat in the vanilla.
Whisk the flour, baking powder and salt together in a bowl. Add to the wet mixture and mix on low speed until just combined.
Cover and chill for at least 1 hour, until firm enough to roll.
Heat the oven to 175°C (155°C fan). Line a baking sheet with baking paper. Put the icing sugar in a small bowl.

Roll the dough into balls 4 to 4.5 cm across, about the size of a golf ball (40 to 60 g, or 2 to 3 tablespoons of dough each), or use a cookie scoop. Smaller balls make 12 cookies, bigger ones 8. Roll each in icing sugar until well coated, and space 5 cm apart on the sheet. Only coat as many as will fit; keep the rest of the dough in the fridge.
Bake for 10 to 12 minutes (a minute or two more for bigger balls), until the edges are set and the centres are puffed but still look wet between the cracks.
Cool on the sheet for a few minutes, then move to a wire rack to cool completely. The centres sink as they cool. Let the sheet cool before the next batch.
Underbake rather than overbake for a fudgy centre.
Doubles easily for a bigger batch.
Warm dough spreads, so keep it cold while you work.
For a mocha version, beat ½ teaspoon instant espresso powder in with the sugar and oil.
Keeps for a week in an airtight container. Freeze unbaked balls on a tray, then bag them; thaw in the fridge for 2 hours before coating and baking.
